findings.text: Memory abort dispatcher accepts fault address plus status plus register context, looks up a descriptor selected by low status bits, invokes its handler first, and on unhandled cases terminates kernel context through a fatal path while delivering a signal with untagged address to user context.

Alignment fault reporter for stack and program counter accepts address plus status plus register context and forwards a SIGBUS notification with BUS_ADRALN code through the generic die notification path.

Kernel undefined instruction handler reads the instruction word at the saved program counter, offers SSBS emulation a chance to consume it, resumes on successful emulation, and otherwise terminates with a fatal undefined instruction diagnostic.

SSBS emulation predicate compares an instruction word under mask against an expected pattern for a system status update, adjusts PSR_SSBS_BIT according to PSTATE_Imm_shift field, skips the faulting instruction on match, and reports whether emulation applied.
BTI, GCS, and FPAC handlers for kernel context provide fatal termination paths; BTI first consults an EFI runtime fixup that on success clears BTYPE state and resumes execution.
MOPS handler for kernel context resets extension procedure state derived from user register state and status, then advances kernel single step sequencing.

Breakpoint and watchpoint dispatchers plus a suspended step resumption helper form the debug trap interface, matching per CPU slots, notifying perf, and sequencing user versus kernel single step state.

Synchronous, interrupt, fast interrupt, and error vectors for 64-bit kernel entry provide architectural trap entry with register context, reading esr_el1 where needed before delegating to second level handlers.

Synchronous vector decodes EC from fault status and routes ESR_ELx_EC_DABT_CUR with ESR_ELx_EC_IABT_CUR to abort handling, ESR_ELx_EC_PC_ALIGN to alignment handling, ESR_ELx_EC_SYS64 with ESR_ELx_EC_UNKNOWN to undefined handling, plus ESR_ELx_EC_BTI and ESR_ELx_EC_GCS and ESR_ELx_EC_MOPS and ESR_ELx_EC_BREAKPT_CUR and ESR_ELx_EC_SOFTSTP_CUR and ESR_ELx_EC_WATCHPT_CUR and ESR_ELx_EC_BRK64 and ESR_ELx_EC_FPAC to dedicated handlers, with unlisted values taking a panic path.

Abort, alignment, undefined, BTI, GCS, MOPS, and FPAC wrappers share kernel mode entry and exit discipline with interrupt state inheritance and delegation to second level handlers; abort and alignment variants capture far_el1 state before entry.

Breakpoint, single step, watchpoint, and BRK64 wrappers use debug specific kernel entry and exit with explicit debug exception bracketing; watchpoint handling captures far_el1 state, while single step handling consults an erratum workaround and suspended breakpoint resumption before fresh single step dispatch.

Interrupt vectors set DAIF_PROCCTX_NOIRQ then select nonmaskable versus normal paths based on configuration and saved interrupt state; error vector restores DAIF_ERRCTX and brackets system error dispatch with nonmaskable entry and exit.
Fault descriptor selection masks the status word with ESR_ELx_FSC and offsets into a table base, so only low status bits influence the choice.
User visible fault address and watchpoint distance evaluation use untagged form, avoiding exposure of tag bits when fault type is unrecognized or marked UNKNOWN.

Unhandled kernel memory faults follow a fixed order of stabilizing spin state, emitting an alert with message and address, invoking a noncanonical hook, decoding abort status, displaying page table entries, terminating with fatal context, restoring spin state, and marking the task dead.
Memory abort diagnostics report status word, EC with mnemonic and IL width, SET with FnV, EA with S1PTW, and FSC with mnemonic, delegating to data abort detail when the class indicates a data abort.

Data abort diagnostics distinguish ISV set versus clear. Set case reports SAS derived size with SSE, SRT, SF, AR, and Xs. Clear case reports raw ISS and ISS2. Both cases report CM, WnR, TnD, TagAccess, GCS, Overlay, and DirtyBit.

Page table display selects address space by range, using current active space for low addresses with a swapper warning, initial space for high addresses, and warning without walking for intermediate addresses.

After announcing table type with page size, address width, and physical base, display walks PGD through P4D, PUD, PMD, and PTE stages, printing raw entry values and stopping early on missing or malformed entries or unmappable final entry.
Physical base for initial address space uses __pa_symbol translation, while other spaces use virt_to_phys translation of the top directory pointer.

Breakpoint scan iterates configured breakpoint count, skips empty slots, requires value register equality with aligned instruction address, decodes control to verify length coverage of low address bits, records trigger on match, and requests stepping only for default overflow handling.

Watchpoint scan iterates configured watchpoint count, skips empty slots, requires access direction compatibility between ESR_ELx_WNR indication and configured type, evaluates untagged distance under length mask, reports exact matches immediately, and otherwise attributes to nearest slot when at least one slot lies within finite nonzero distance.

Watchpoint reporting records trigger address and follows default overflow indication, except user privileged events firing in kernel context force stepping without perf notification while other cases notify perf.

Control toggling applies only to requested breakpoint versus watchpoint class whose privilege maps to requested exception level, leaving other slots untouched, and flips only the enable bit through read modify write.
Privilege mapping accepts exactly AARCH64_BREAKPOINT_EL0 with AARCH64_BREAKPOINT_EL1 for respective exception levels and treats other values as invalid with warning and error indication.

Debug register access dispatches on sum of class base and slot index across AARCH64_DBG_REG_BVR with AARCH64_DBG_REG_BCR plus AARCH64_DBG_REG_WVR with AARCH64_DBG_REG_WCR, each covering sixteen indices, warns on out of range selection, returns zero on invalid reads, and issues a barrier after writes.

Breakpoint trap holds per slot read side critical sections during inspection, watchpoint trap holds one critical section across full scan, and page table display holds an interrupt save guard across lockless walk with single copy reads of each level.
Fault descriptor entries logically provide a handler returning a handled indication, a textual name, and signal number with code used for user notification and diagnostics.

Per thread debug state logically holds disabled flags for breakpoints and watchpoints plus a suspended step flag; per counter state logically holds trigger address with control privilege and length plus type for access matching.

User breakpoint and watchpoint stepping disables corresponding register class, records disabled state, and either marks suspension when single step is already active or enables single step; completion reenables disabled classes and either resumes suspended stepping or disables single step.

Kernel stepping uses a per CPU marker with ARM_KERNEL_STEP_NONE, ARM_KERNEL_STEP_ACTIVE, and ARM_KERNEL_STEP_SUSPEND. Fresh traps with no active single step become active and enable single step, traps during active single step become suspended, reentry while non none returns early, and completion reenables kernel classes plus user watchpoints unless user watchpoints remain disabled, then either disables single step or propagates suspension before clearing the marker.

Single step vector first offers an erratum handler a chance to consume the exception; only when declined does it bracket debug handling and prefer resuming suspended breakpoints over dispatching fresh single step events.

Diagnostic page table walk observes live tables without address space locks, so concurrent modification can yield inconsistent levels; mitigation is limited to interrupt suppression and single copy reads, and display must not drive fault resolution.

When no exact watchpoint match exists, attribution falls back to closest slot by untagged distance, which can misattribute spurious addresses to an unrelated watchpoint when any slot lies within finite distance.

Kernel accesses can trigger user privileged watchpoints, so kernel watchpoint handling always disables user watchpoint registers even for kernel mode traps to avoid immediate retrigger through unprivileged paths.
Alignment faults use SIGBUS with BUS_ADRALN, and unrecoverable kernel memory faults terminate with SIGKILL.
Debug register file exposes AARCH64_DBG_REG_BVR with AARCH64_DBG_REG_BCR plus AARCH64_DBG_REG_WVR with AARCH64_DBG_REG_WCR, each with sixteen indexed slots addressed by base plus index.
Instruction breakpoint comparison aligns address to four byte boundary for value matching and uses low two address bits as selector against decoded length mask for byte confirmation.
